A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same B-PAC reasoning work. All 25 pages of each version, including Appendices A-D, are readable; equations, tables, figures, and relocated content support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original benchmark comparisons, distribution-shift experiments, and ablations measuring risk, expert calls, and token consumption.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by uncertainty-score experiments in Table 2 and a computational-cost measurement in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The routing, IPS estimator, wealth updates, adaptive betting, and exploration rules remain unchanged. The new perplexity and entropy tests use the existing score-agnostic method. The practical recommendation to use Equation (7) does not establish a procedural change: v1 Appendix C.3 already specified it for all experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MATH, MMLU-Pro, BBH, and Magpie, including the same mixed-stream scenarios. The additional score tests use existing datasets and tasks; the revised mixture sample counts concern experimental settings.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain PAC reasoning, O-Naive, IPS+Hoeff, Chain of Draft, and NoThinking. The newly mentioned bootstrap/random-weighting alternative is not evaluated. Perplexity and entropy are B-PAC score variants, not added competing methods.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 changes the reported Figure 2 mixture from 1,500 BBH plus 3,000 MMLU-Pro samples to 1,500 MMLU-Pro plus 3,000 BBH samples. This is a reported setting revision; the unchanged figure does not establish a rerun. Appendix D.1 adds score substitutions while retaining the other experimental settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.1 tests sensitivity to uncertainty-score choice using perplexity and entropy on Magpie and MMLU-Pro. The tolerance, betting-strategy, exploration-strategy, and warm-up analyses remain, with the previous Appendix D subsections renumbered.

E5.justification: The existing 100-repeat statement and standard-deviation bands remain. Table 2 extends mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting to new results without introducing a different uncertainty-estimation practice or reporting increased repetitions, new seeds, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds four ER/ECP/TP result rows. For example, Magpie with perplexity reports ER 0.0551, ECP 22.76%, and TP 61.69%. Appendix A.3 newly reports 0.046 seconds for 1,000 requests. Table 1 values and the existing plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Remark C.3 defines risk incorporating judge noise and states a safety extension for i.i.d. noise independent of queries. It relates this risk to the original risk under zero-mean additive noise. The principal safety and regret theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central novelty, anytime-safety, logarithmic-regret, and efficiency claims remain, including the abstract's reduction of thinking-model usage by up to 81.01%. The added broader-routing paragraph proposes future applicability without changing the principal demonstrated contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds an interpretation of Theorem 5.1 as a worst-case guarantee and recommends Equation (7) empirically for nonstationary deployment. It also acknowledges potentially stronger UCB baselines, discusses judge noise reducing efficiency, and suggests broader routing applications. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 6 adds a reproduction-code link. Appendix A.3 replaces the brief constant-time/microsecond description with a concrete timing report and an explanation of scalar updates over the threshold grid. Existing model configurations, hardware, and principal hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Ming et al. random-weighting reference and cites it in Appendix C.3 when discussing potentially tighter UCB baselines. The main related-work discussion and positioning against offline PAC reasoning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, expands several explanatory paragraphs, updates affiliations and the conference footer, and adds acknowledgements. Appendix D gains a subsection, but the overall narrative and section organization remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 2, relocates Figures 1-3 through page reflow, and corrects Figure 5's duplicated panel labels and malformed tolerance value. Existing plots retain their graphical contents, and the overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: Table 2 supplies additional empirical support for flexibility in uncertainty-score choice, while the code link and concrete overhead report improve reproducibility information. The judge-noise discussion adds useful conditional reasoning. These gains are limited: the main evidence and theory remain largely unchanged, and implementation details for the new scores and timing measurement remain sparse.
